entries.snippet: The requested changes are related to the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of highly enriched uranium, according to US media.

entries.title: A cancer vaccine made just for you. mRNA is back and it's fighting melanoma
entries.snippet: A study finds that an mRNA vaccine is highly effective at preventing recurrence of this dangerous skin cancer, when used in combination with Keytruda, an immunotherapy drug.

entries.title: U.S. strikes Iranian military sites. And, Trump's $1.8 billion fund faces scrutiny
entries.snippet: American aircraft fired on a number of Iranian sites over the weekend, including Qeeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. And, Trump's anti-weaponization fund faces scrutiny in Congress and the courts.

entries.title: Confirmed Ebola cases in Congo reach 282 as survivors describe their recoveries
entries.snippet: The outbreak remains focused in Congo's eastern Ituri province. Congo has reported over 1,000 suspected cases with the Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved treatment or vaccine.

entries.title: 'At what point does it make sense to ditch a gas car for an electric vehicle?'
entries.snippet: "At what point does it make sense to ditch a gas car for an EV?" NPR listener Guadalupe Higuera of Phoenix asked this question and worked with Climate Desk reporter Jeff Brady to answer it.

entries.title: Is bovine colostrum really 'liquid gold' for gut health?
entries.snippet: Baby calves rely on it to build up their immune systems and gut. And now marketers are promoting it for humans. Here's what scientists say.

entries.title: One by one, U.S. civil rights agency dismantles tools to fight discrimination
entries.snippet: The EEOC is seeking to overturn rules created decades ago to tackle discrimination in employment. The Trump administration says those rules have led to more discrimination —against white people.

entries.title: Morning news brief

entries.title: Violent clashes give way to peaceful PSG parade after Champions League win
entries.snippet: A huge crowd of supporters gathered peacefully near the Eiffel Tower on Sunday to celebrate Paris Saint-Germain's victory, which was marred by violent clashes overnight that led police to detain hundreds of people.

entries.title: Right-wing candidate pulls ahead in first round of Colombia's presidential vote
entries.snippet: Tough-on-crime outsider Aberaldo de la Espriella took the lead in Colombia's presidential race on Sunday night, setting up a runoff with Iván Cepeda, an ally of outgoing President Gustavo Petro.

entries.title: U.S. bombs Iranian military sites and Kuwait is hit by drone and missile fire
entries.snippet: The U.S. military says it bombed Iranian radar and drone control sites in Iran after Tehran shot down an American MQ-1 Predator drone this weekend. Kuwait said its air defenses opened fire on Monday.

entries.title: Standoff between Republicans and White House over the 'anti-weaponization' fund remains unresolved
entries.snippet: Senate Republicans say they won't have the votes for the immigration spending bill until the White House works with them to put some parameters on a new $1.776 billion settlement fund designed to compensate Trump's allies — or scrap it altogether.

entries.title: Polls close in Colombia vote with Espriella and Cepeda advancing to runoff
entries.snippet: Lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella and peace-builder Iván Cepeda were leading the vote counts in the first round of Colombia's presidential elections on Sunday, and are to face off in a presidential runoff in the South American nation later in June.

entries.title: Platner's wife calls reports about Senate candidate's explicit texts with women 'shameful'
entries.snippet: Graham Platner's wife called reports that her husband had previously exchanged sexually explicit text messages with several women "shameful" over the weekend, the latest controversy to hit the Maine Democrat's whirlwind campaign.

entries.title: Older Americans often compelled to keep working — and face criticism for doing so
entries.snippet: Over the past several decades, demographic and economic changes have significantly altered how people experience work and aging.

entries.title: Indigenous rights leader Brooklyn Rivera dies after nearly 3 years detained in Nicaragua
entries.snippet: Brooklyn Rivera, a renowned Indigenous leader from Nicaragua who spent years fighting for the rights of his community and was imprisoned by the government in September 2023, has died.

entries.title: Farmers seek fertilizer alternatives as Iran war drives up prices
entries.snippet: Since the Iran war began on Feb. 28, fertilizer prices have risen by 40%.

entries.title: Experimental drug shows promise against deadly pancreatic cancer
entries.snippet: A novel pill helped people with advanced pancreatic cancer live longer, researchers reported Sunday, raising hopes of long-needed better treatments for one of the deadliest types of cancer.

entries.title: Recovering wetlands fuel growth of flamingo population in Venice
entries.snippet: The pale pink birds — called "fenicotteri" in Italian — are now flocking to Venice in record numbers, as ecological efforts to restore damaged wetlands could help expand their habitat and possibly induce them to nest in the lagoon.

entries.title: WHO chief reports 5 Ebola recoveries as new treatment center opens in Congo
entries.snippet: Five patients have recovered from a rare type of Ebola virus, the head of the World Health Organization said Sunday during a visit to Bunia in eastern Congo.

entries.title: Hundreds detained in France after violence erupts following Paris Saint-Germain victory
entries.snippet: A huge crowd of supporters gathered peacefully near the Eiffel Tower on Sunday to celebrate Paris Saint-Germain's second Champions League title victory, which was marred by violent clashes overnight across France and led police to detain hundreds of people.

entries.title: Israeli troops seize strategic castle in Lebanon during deepest incursion in decades
entries.snippet: Israeli troops have captured a strategic mountain topped with a Crusader-built castle in southern Lebanon in the deepest incursion into the country in more than a quarter-century, the military said Sunday.

entries.title: Do you need SPF 30, 50 or 100? Dermatologists answer your burning sunscreen questions
entries.snippet: PolitiFact asked board-certified dermatologists to answer people's burning questions about SPF. When it comes to sunscreen, they advised buying broad-spectrum sunscreen that's SPF 30 or higher and reapplying regularly.

entries.title: Trump plans to appeal ruling letting importers seek refunds of paid struck-down tariffs
entries.snippet: Businesses big and small have started receiving tariff refunds after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that President Trump lacked the constitutional authority to impose higher import taxes on goods from nearly every other country.

entries.title: Fact-checking Trump on National Mall's Reflecting Pool renovations
entries.snippet: As President Donald Trump delves into several projects to remake the monumental core of the nation's capital, PolitiFact fact-checks statements he's made about renovations he's ordered for the National Mall's Reflecting Pool.

entries.title: Bus driver charged after Virginia crash kills 5, including family headed to wedding
entries.snippet: A family of four from Massachusetts who were killed when a bus crashed into multiple vehicles in Virginia were traveling to a wedding with a carload of homemade desserts for the celebration.

entries.title: Colombia accuses Ecuador of interfering in its general election
entries.snippet: Colombia's government rejected a move by Ecuador's president to eliminate tariffs on Colombian imports because of a tariff commitment made to an opposition candidate, calling it "deliberate interference" in the ongoing electoral process.

entries.title: U.S. says it stopped a merchant ship trying to breach blockade and reach Iran
entries.snippet: The U.S. military stopped a merchant vessel trying to break through its blockade of Iranian ports by firing a missile into its engine room, the U.S. Central Command said on Saturday.

entries.title: Four men rescued from flooded Laos cave as search continues for 2 others
entries.snippet: Rescue workers in Laos said Saturday they have safely evacuated four villagers trapped in a flooded cave for 10 days.

entries.title: Autopsy planned for dead humpback whale brought ashore in Denmark
entries.snippet: The carcass of a humpback whale, whose life and death captivated Germans for months as the mammal became repeatedly stranded in the Baltic Sea, was dragged Saturday onto a Danish beach.

entries.title: Coups and crises shake African democracy

entries.title: Can Iran rebuild trust with its Gulf neighbors?
entries.snippet: Mutual suspicion between Iran and Persian Gulf countries is poised to affect regional stability, growth and cooperation years into the future.

entries.title: Mozart the idol: Searching for beauty in times of crisis
entries.snippet: Mozart's music evokes lightness and beauty. In times of war and destruction, people often invoke the ideals of the classical era. But is this just an escape from reality? The Mozartfest Würzburg offers different answers.

entries.title: Hungary's PM Peter Magyar moves to oust president
entries.snippet: Hungary's new Prime Minister, Peter Magyar, has moved to oust the president, threatening constitutional action. Head of state Tamas Sulyok has refused Magyar's demand that he resign.

entries.title: India news: 'Cockroach' party founder plans protests
entries.snippet: Abhijeet Dipke says he will return to India on June 6. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi has alleged 'fraud' in exam markings, and Virat Kohli has fired Bengaluru to the IPL title. DW has more.

entries.title: Taiwan opposition leader heads to US
entries.snippet: KMT leader Cheng Li-wun is traveling to the US for a two-week visit. She has indicated she is "very interested" in meeting President Donald Trump but could face a grilling over her stance on China relations.

entries.title: Mozambique: Are 'death squads' targeting the opposition?
entries.snippet: Deadly violence against opposition politicians has shaken Mozambique. While the government has called the incidents isolated cases, opposition and civil society warn of a pattern of politically motivated assassinations.

entries.title: Germany news: Migration to Germany falls sharply in 2025
entries.snippet: Fewer migrants are making their way to Germany, with net migration dropping to nearly half what is was. Meanwhile, a court in Düsseldorf has sentenced a man to life in prison over an Islamist attack. DW has the latest.

entries.title: How China keeps North Korea's economy alive
entries.snippet: Pyongyang relies on China for 95% of its legitimate trade; hacking, arms deals and remittances also help it stay afloat.

entries.title: Young German talents impress in World Cup tune-up vs Finland
entries.snippet: Deniz Undav and Lennart Karl delivered strong performances in Germany's last game at home before the start of 2026 FIFA World Cup.

entries.title: France intercepts Russian-linked oil tanker in Atlantic
entries.snippet: France has intercepted a sanctioned tanker in the Atlantic Ocean as it steps up efforts to target Russia's "shadow fleet." Naval officials said the ship was sailing under a false flag.

entries.title: The German town cutting emissions with play cash
entries.snippet: It started as a school project to promote local businesses in a remote Bavarian region. Now, the "Chiemgauer" currency helps to cut emissions.

entries.title: Ethiopia votes as ruling party eyes landslide win
entries.snippet: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's party is running unopposed in several constituencies. Opposition parties have warned that the elections are even less open than previous votes.

entries.title: US and Iran trade strikes as diplomatic efforts continue
entries.snippet: The US bombed radar and drone sites in Iran and Tehran attacked a US air base in Kuwait. Follow live.

entries.title: DNA had one rule. Bacteria didn't get the memo

entries.title: Nicaragua: Indigenous leader Brooklyn Rivera dies in detention
entries.snippet: The Indigenous leader and former lawmaker had been detained by Nicaragua's authoritarian government in 2023 on undisclosed charges.

entries.title: US: Newark mayor orders curfew after Delaney Hall protests
entries.snippet: The authorities have faced days of protest by pro-immigrant groups at the Delaney Hall detention center in New Jersey, with the center's residents reportedly on a hunger strike over living conditions in the facility.

entries.title: Colombia set for runoff vote after tight presidential poll
entries.snippet: Right-wing outsider Abelardo de la Espreilla seems set to face veteran leftist candidate Ivan Cepeda in the second round of the Colombia presidential election, but Cepeda seemed to question the preliminary results.

entries.title: Germany news: Most expect AfD state premier after elections
entries.snippet: Most people in Germany expect a premier from the far-right AfD to lead at least one state after elections in the autumn, a survey has found. The Brenner Pass linking Austria and Italy has reopened.
